stage_a.note: Smiling and enthusiastically showing the product options.
Clasping hands, leaning forward, speaking with an excited tone.
Smiling warmly while showing a picture of his child.

venture.description: Edible organic food paint and condiments in tubes for kids to draw on their food.
venture.note: Licensing deals with Crayola, Peppa Pig, and others.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 presents Noshi, edible food paint for kids, and asks for $250,000 for 17% equity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 handles the product and remarks why not.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 names the different branded boxes of food paint.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks if he has a deal with Crayola since it is branded.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms licensing deals with Peppa Pig, Crayola, and others.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 notes he likes that F1 likes royalty deals.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 jokes he is not averse to royalty deals.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 remarks that it does not seem like a lot of ketchup for a kid.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the box has three tubes and one tube is enough for a meal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks what the container sells for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says it sells for $5.46.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 repeats the price to confirm.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks what it costs to make.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says $2.72, but machinery from the investment would reduce the cost by 60 cents.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the wholesale price of the box of three.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says the wholesale price is $3.70.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 comments that the margins are awful.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 says he must have sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states last year's sales were $117,000.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what he thinks sales will be this year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 projects $200,000 by the end of the year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks why sales are so small and how many stores he is in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers they are in 370 Walmart stores.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how much he is selling online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains he hasn't sold any online because his wife has had long COVID for three years.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks to clarify if it has been three years.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms and adds he has been raising his two children almost as a single parent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks to confirm she is a long hauler in COVID.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms, adding she had a successful career but likely won't work again.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks where he is based.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says New York, and explains his wife moved back to England to be cared for.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 comments that must be horrible.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees it is terrible but his priority is keeping his kids happy and healthy.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks what he was doing before this happened.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 recounts growing up in England, moving to New York, and his career before becoming a stay-at-home parent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if the $20,000 in sales was out of all those stores.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms, explaining people didn't know what it was because he designed the packaging poorly.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks to see the sales trajectory from 2018.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says 2018 to 2020 were all flat because the packaging was wrong.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if he stayed in those retailers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says they came out of Safeway and Albertsons in 2018 and got into Walmart in 2019.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks how Walmart feels about how they are selling.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says Walmart is putting Sketchup into 1,500 stores next year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if they are currently selling through.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms the last three production runs are the first they have sold through completely.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 says that is a good sign.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 exits, citing the lack of sales, flat trajectory, and not wanting to take on a job.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks Kevin despite being sad to hear his decision.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 exits, feeling the product belongs in a gift aisle rather than a food aisle.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 acknowledges her decision, calling it a shame.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 exits, thinking it is a clever idea but not seeing enough to make an offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks Lori for her time.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits, believing the six-dollar price point per meal is causing sales resistance.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks Daymond.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks Mark if there is nothing he can do to convince him.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 explains the hard part is shelf presence and needing to grab attention quickly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks Mark for saying the Crayola packaging is cool.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 suggests Crayola will get more attention, but online sales will be far more important.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees that online is where the money will be made.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what he will do to get online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains he needs funds to produce the product to sell online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 pleads with Mark to help him out.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 jokes about the Walmart expansion to prod Mark.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if he would consider selling them as one-offs so people can try them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 adds that a basket of single flavors for $1.99 would be easier for parents to pick up.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says he is open to doing anything and knew it was a good idea.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 offers $250,000 for 25% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 immediately accepts Mark's offer.

decisions.note: Lack of sales, flat trajectory, one-man show, doesn't want a job.
Believes it belongs in a gift aisle, not the food aisle, doesn't see it as a competitive food item.
Clever idea, but not enough there for her to make an offer today.
Great novelty, but $6 every meal is too much, causing sales resistance.
Thinks the Crayola branding is cool and suggests selling single tubes.
